title: The optimal polynomial lower bound on the edge-isoperimetric number of the graph square
author: Aida Abiad, Nils van de Berg, Emanuel Juliano, Harper Reijnders, Robin Simoens, Thijs van Veluw and Jim Wittebol
work: The edge-isoperimetric number of graphs and their powers
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 3.7 of the article (source label theorem:lowerboundi(G^2)closed, source0.tex lines 357--367), the optimal closed-form lower bound on the edge-isoperimetric number $i(G^2)$ of the square of a non-complete regular connected graph, with its three cases for the optimal polynomial $p$ distinguished by the spectral quantities $\Lambda$, $M$, $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_2$ and $\lambda_n$. It is delivered with the authors' own complete 59-line proof at source0.tex lines 370--428. H2: the proof is a genuine optimisation of a spectral bound rather than a qualifying examination exercise. The solver must take the general polynomial $p=ax^2+bx+c$, translate the isoperimetric inequality of the general theorem into the three candidate regimes for the coefficients through the interlacing eigenvalues of $G^2$, compare the resulting rational expressions one by one, and identify in each case the polynomial that makes the bound sharp, obtaining the three displayed inequalities. Reproducing that case analysis of spectral bounds for the graph square is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
